subject: Music Production
title: Absorption and Acoustic Treatment
description: A micro-lesson that makes Absorption and Acoustic Treatment usable.

hook.text: Hard surfaces reflect sound, but soft materials like foam and fabric absorb it instead.

buildup.text: Acoustic panels placed on studio walls trap reflections and prevent them from reaching microphones.

discovery.text: A well-treated room gives producers a clean, neutral listening space for accurate mixing.

twist.text: Over-treating a room makes it sound eerily dead, which is uncomfortable for performers.

climax.text: Professional studios balance absorption and reflection to create controlled, pleasant-sounding rooms.

punchline.text: Foam on walls gives producers sonic truth.

quiz.question: What happens when a studio room is over-treated with absorption?
options: It sounds eerily dead and uncomfortable
